chapter: Ellington, the South, bebop and radio
title: Dizzy and Charlie Parker at Monroe's Uptown House
summary: He lived above Monroe's Uptown House, heard Dizzy and Parker through the floor, jammed with them and tried to adjust to their fast different style.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Well, they used to... I used to hear them at a place on 134th Street... Monroe's...

Monroe's Uptown House, which was down in the basement. That's... In fact, that's where Campanella's Whiskey Store is now. I used to... I lived right up on the second floor or something, and I lived right in that area where you could hear the music coming straight up. I used to go down there and jam. That's when I met Dizzy and... I guess I had met Dizzy before. But I became very acquainted with his thing and Charlie's thing, because I lived right upstairs and I could hear the whole thing. You know, I used to go down and jam some with them.
Did what they were doing then sound like they were trying to be different, or...?
Yeah, they was playing a different type of thing, you know.
Did it strike you as something that you thought would spread out the way that it did?

Well, it was spreading then. I liked it. I thought it was all right. You just had to adjust yourself to a certain kind of thing. I couldn't do it too well, to tell you the truth. I didn't have the skill they had, you know. But I tried.
Were they into a lot of fast tempos then and stuff?
Yeah, they used to play a lot of fast tempos.
